stem: The vapour density of fully dissociated NH 4 Cl would be (a) Less than half of the vapour density of pure NH 4 Cl (b) Double of the vapour density of pure NH 4 Cl (c) Half of the vapour density of pure NH 4 Cl (d) One-third of the vapour density of pure NH 4 Cl

stem: At the equilibrium of the reaction N 2 O 4 (g) ⇌ 2NO 2 (g) the observed molar mass of N 2 O 4 is 77.70 g. The percentage dissociation of N 2 O 4 is (a) 28.4 (b) 46.7 (c) 22.4 (d) 18.4
Given X ⇌ nY (in one litre vessel), starting from 1 mol of X. If the degree of dissociation is α, then Kc is (a) nαⁿ/(1−α) (b) nα/(1−α) (c) (nα)ⁿ/(1+α) (d) (nα)ⁿ/(1−α)

In the equilibrium AB ⇌ A + B, if the equilibrium concentration of A is doubled (the equilibrium concentration of AB remaining the same), the equilibrium concentration of B would become (a) Twice (b) Half (c) 1/4th (d) 1/8th

In a system A(s) ⇌ 2B(g) + 3C(g), if the concentration of C at equilibrium is increased by a factor of 2, it will cause the equilibrium concentration of B to change to (a) Two times the original value (b) One half of its original value (c) 2√2 times the original value (d) 1/(2√2) times the original value

Given the reaction A(g) + B(g) ⇌ 2C(g) + D(g). One mole of A and one mole of B are placed in a 1.0 litre vessel. After equilibrium has been established, 0.4 mole of C is present in the vessel. Calculate K c for the reaction.

The equilibrium constant for the reaction CO(g) + H 2 O(g) ⇌ CO 2 (g) + H 2 (g) at a certain temperature is 2.2. Initially one mole of CO and one mole of H 2 O are placed in a 2.0 L container. What are the concentrations of all the substances when the reaction reaches equilibrium?

What method is used to determine α from vapour density data? (a) Dumas method (b) Ideal gas law (c) Vapour density method (d) Gravimetric analysis

A gas AB 2 dissociates according to the reaction AB 2 ⇌ A + 2B. The theoretical molar mass is M = 90 g/mol and the observed molar mass at equilibrium is m = 75 g/mol. If n = 3, find the degree of dissociation (x). Formula: x = (M − m)/[(n − 1) × m] (a) 0.10 (b) 0.15 (c) 0.20 (d) 0.25
A gas PCl 5 dissociates into PCl 3 + Cl 2 . M = 208 g/mol, m = 190 g/mol at equilibrium, n = 2. Calculate x. Formula: x = (M − m)/[(n − 1) × m] (a) 0.08 (b) 0.09 (c) 0.10 (d) 0.12
A gaseous molecule X 2 Y 4 dissociates into 2XY 2 . Vapour density changes from 100 to 80. If n = 2, find x. Formula: x = (D − d)/[(n − 1) × d] (a) 0.20 (b) 0.25 (c) 0.30 (d) 0.40
A gas P 2 dissociates into 2P. The molar mass of P 2 is 60 g/mol, but at equilibrium it is found to be 50 g/mol. If n = 2, find x. Formula: x = (M − m)/[(n − 1) m] (a) 0.18 (b) 0.20 (c) 0.25 (d) 0.30

A gaseous molecule AB dissociates into A + B with n = 2. Its theoretical molar mass is 80 g/mol. If x = 0.25, find the molar mass at equilibrium m. Formula: m = M/[1 + x(n − 1)] (a) 64 g/mol (b) 66 g/mol (c) 70 g/mol (d) 72 g/mol

A diatomic molecule X 2 dissociates into 2X. Its initial vapour density is 48. If n = 2 and x = 0.10, find its vapour density at equilibrium d. Formula: d = D/[1 + x(n − 1)] (a) 44 (b) 45 (c) 46 (d) 47

A gas Q 2 dissociates into 2Q. Its equilibrium molar mass is 72 g/mol and the degree of dissociation is x = 0.25. If n = 2, find the theoretical molar mass M. Formula: M = m[1 + x(n − 1)] (a) 88 g/mol (b) 90 g/mol (c) 92 g/mol (d) 94 g/mol

A gas A 2 B 2 dissociates according to the equation A 2 B 2 → 2AB. The initial molar mass is 90 g/mol and at equilibrium it is 75 g/mol. If n = 2, find x. Formula: x = (M − m)/[(n − 1) × m] (a) 0.18 (b) 0.20 (c) 0.25 (d) 0.28

For a gas reaction 3H 2 + N 2 ⇌ 2NH 3 , the partial pressures of H 2 and N 2 are 0.4 and 0.8 atmosphere respectively. The total pressure of the entire system is 2.8 atmosphere. What will be the value of K p if all the concentrations are given in atmospheres?

If the concentrations of N 2 , H 2 and NH 3 are 1, 2 and 3 respectively, their concentrations at equilibrium will be, for N 2 + 3H 2 ⇌ 2NH 3 : (a) (1−x), (2−3x), 2x (b) (1−x/3), (2−x), 2x/3 (c) (1−x), (2−x), (3+x) (d) (1−x), (2−3x), (3+2x)

Acetic acid undergoes dimerization when dissolved in benzene: 2CH 3 COOH ⇌ (CH 3 COOH) 2 . The molecular mass of acetic acid is found to be 120. Which among the following relations is correct? (a) α = 2[(D−d)/d] (b) α = 2[(D−d)/D] (c) α = 2[(d−D)/d] (d) α = [2d/(D−d)]

At 627 °C and 1 atm, SO₃ is partially dissociated into SO₂ and O₂ by the reaction SO₃(g) ⇌ SO₂(g) + ½O₂(g). The density of the equilibrium mixture is 0.925 g L⁻¹. What is the degree of dissociation? (Assume ideal behaviour; R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.)

If α is the fraction of HI dissociated at equilibrium in the reaction 2HI ⇌ H 2 + I 2 , then starting with 2 mol of HI, the total number of moles of reactant and products at equilibrium are: (a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 1+α (d) 2+2α
Vapour density of PCl 5 is 104.16 but when heated at 230 °C its vapour density is reduced to 62. The percentage dissociation of PCl 5 at this temperature will be: (a) 6.8% (b) 68% (c) 46% (d) 64%

At 200 °C, a compound ‘A’ (molar mass = 100 g mol −1 ) in the vapour phase dissociates as A(g) → 2B(g) + C(g). The vapour density of the vapour at 200 °C is found to be 30. The percent dissociation of the compound A at 200 °C will be: (a) 33% (b) 66% (c) 87% (d) 100%
At a certain temperature and total pressure of 10 5 Pa, iodine vapour contains 40% by volume of I atoms: I 2 (g) ⇌ 2I(g). Calculate K p for the equilibrium.

stem: 0.6 mole of NH 3 in a reaction vessel of 2 dm 3 capacity was brought to equilibrium. The vessel was then found to contain 0.15 mole of H 2 formed by the reaction 2NH 3 (g) ⇌ N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g). Which of the following statements is true? (a) 0.15 mole of the original NH 3 had dissociated at equilibrium (b) 0.55 mole of ammonia is left in the vessel (c) At equilibrium the vessel contained 0.45 mole of N 2 (d) The concentration of NH 3 at equilibrium is 0.25 mole per dm 3
book_key: (d) The concentration of NH₃ at equilibrium is 0.25 mole per dm³

stem: The equilibrium constant K p for the reaction 2SO 2 + O 2 ⇌ 2SO 3 at 1000 K is 3.5. The partial pressure of oxygen gas to give equal moles of SO 2 and SO 3 is: (a) 0.29 atm (b) 3.5 atm (c) 0.53 atm (d) 1.87 atm

Ammonium hydrogen sulphide dissociates according to the equation NH 4 HS(s) ⇌ NH 3 (g) + H 2 S(g). If the observed pressure at equilibrium is 1.12 atm at 380 K, what is the equilibrium constant K p of the reaction?

In the equilibrium SO 2 Cl 2 ⇌ SO 2 + Cl 2 at 2000 K and 10 atm pressure, %Cl 2 = %SO 2 = 40 by volume. Then: (a) K p = 2 atm (b) n(SO 2 Cl 2 )/n(SO 2 ) = 1/4 at equilibrium (c) K p = 8 atm (d) n(SO 2 Cl 2 ) = n(SO 2 ) = n(Cl 2 )

Given: ΔG°f(N₂O₄) = 100 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔG°f(NO₂) = 50 kJ mol⁻¹. Find ΔG of the reaction at 298 K. (Ideal gases, standard state 1 bar, R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.)

The dissociation equilibrium of a gas AB 2 can be represented as 2AB 2 (g) ⇌ 2AB(g) + B 2 (g). The degree of dissociation is ‘x’ and is small compared to 1. The expression relating the degree of dissociation (x) with equilibrium constant K p and total pressure P is: (a) (2K p /P) (b) (2K p /P) 1/3 (c) (2K p /P) 1/2 (d) (K p /P)

The dissociation of PCl 5 takes place as PCl 5 (g) ⇌ PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g). If the degree of dissociation is α at equilibrium pressure P, then the equilibrium constant for the reaction is: (a) K p = α 2 /(1+α 2 P) (b) K p = α 2 P 2 /(1−α 2 ) (c) K p = αP 2 /(1−α 2 ) (d) K p = α 2 P/(1−α 2 )

The equilibrium constants for the reactions X ⇌ 2Y and Z ⇌ P + Q are K 1 and K 2 respectively. If the initial concentrations and the degree of dissociation of X and Z are the same, the ratio K 1 /K 2 is: (a) 4 (b) 1 (c) 0.5 (d) 2

After decomposition at constant volume in a vessel the pressure increases to 45 atm. What is the percentage of ammonia dissociated?
